newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian UGB says may file for bankruptcy Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Belgian UGB says may file for bankruptcy Tuesday.

text.p: Belgian steelmaker Usines Gustave Boel (UGB), which is negotiating an alliance with Dutch steel group Hoogovens, said on Monday it may file for bankruptcy on Tuesday after unions blocked a referendum on the merger plan.
"The option of depositing the accounts cannot be excluded any more. We are getting closer to going for bankruptcy than to a takeover and merger," UGB spokesman Pierre Stievenart told Reuters.
Unions, who had rejected the idea of a referendum, ransacked the voting office in UGB's plant in La Louviere shortly before it was due to start, Stievenart said.
"(President) Pol Boel believes that the referendum cannot take place under normal conditions..." he said.
The alliance with Hoogovens envisages reducing UGB's workforce to 1,200 in the first quarter of 1997 from the current level of around 2,000.
Hoogovens aims to take a 50 percent stake and invest three billion Belgian francs in UGB if there is an accord to restructure the company which is family-owned.
Stievenart said some 100 trade unionists caused several millions of francs worth of damage after bursting into the office where the referendum was to take place.
The workers smashed windows, seized television tapes and burned ballot boxes and wooden panels, he said.
He said that UGB management would address the Brussels commercial court at 0800 GMT on Tuesday at the request of the president of the court.
